terms.gloss: make a plan, form a plan, decide
terms.grammar: phrase: dē with the ablative of what is planned, or ut with the subjunctive
evidence: Caes. BG 3.2: id acciderat, ut Gallī cōnsilium caperent (Lewis & Short s.v. accidō)
Traupman 105: to make plans for the trip, cōnsilium capere dē itinere

phrases.english: What do you think of this plan?
Let’s make plans for the trip.

sources: Lewis & Short: consilium. Dictionary links support the component words; the modern technical expressions are labelled separately.
The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
